Question 7 of 11 · Revelation and the Prophet ﷺ

Who was Muhammad ﷺ?

How to evaluate someone who claims to be a messenger, and what history records about Muhammad ﷺ.

The case

01

Many people throughout history claimed to be messengers from God. How do we evaluate them?

What would make a messenger credible?

02

Muhammad ﷺ was known by his people as 'Al-Amin' — The Trustworthy — before any claim to prophethood.

His enemies never accused him of lying in 40 years before his prophethood.

His character before prophethood

Muhammad ﷺ lived among his people for 40 years before claiming prophethood. Even his fiercest opponents never called him a liar about worldly matters — they rejected his message, not his character.

Read more

Abu Jahl, one of his greatest enemies, once said privately: 'I know you are not lying — but if I follow you, what will the nobles of Quraysh say?'

03

Muhammad ﷺ taught one central message: There is only one God, and humans are accountable for their actions.

He didn't ask people to take it on faith alone — he invited rational examination.

04

The Quran — revealed to an illiterate man — contains knowledge not available in the 7th century.

Unlike other miracles, the Quran can be examined by anyone today.

Objections, answered

The strongest pushback we hear, and our answer to each.

You might say“How do we know he was illiterate?”

Our answer

His illiteracy is historically documented.

What history records

Muhammad ﷺ never attended school, never learned to read or write. This is confirmed by both Muslim and non-Muslim historical sources. The Quran refers to him as 'the unlettered prophet' (Al-Ummiy).
